## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

RaceRecordingRepository — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt

## Trigger

Marking a segment, via SegmentMarkingController.onPressEnd calling
recordingRepository.markSegment — observed, already running in a
ViewModel's coroutine scope. Two more triggers reach the same lock and
need a second gap of their own, below: `findInProgress()` called
directly in `WatchApp`'s composable body (MAIN, PROJECTION, CONTROL
branches, MainActivity.kt lines 177, 192, 204), and
`onComplicationRequest` in `WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService`.

## Today

`RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl` wraps eight of its nine public methods —
every one but `observeRecorded()` — in `synchronized(lock)`. Inside
that block, `markSegment` (lines 78-136) reads the profile with
`runBlocking { profileRepository.observe().first() }` (line 99) to get
`correctionFactor` and `expectedDistanceM` before calling
`CorrectionFactorCalculator.compute`. `ProfileRepository.observe()`
returns `Flow<Profile>` and is otherwise reached as a suspension
everywhere else in the app; here it is blocked on, on whatever thread
calls `markSegment`, while the shared `lock` is held. Every other
public method — `startClock`, `findInProgress`, `undoLastMark`,
`stopRace`, `markSent`, `eraseRecorded`, `findById` — also
synchronizes on the same `lock` object, so a call to any of them
blocks until `markSegment`'s `runBlocking` returns.

Three call sites reach that lock from outside the coroutine
`markSegment` already runs in: `WatchApp`'s composable body calls
`raceRecordingRepository.findInProgress()` directly on the MAIN,
PROJECTION and CONTROL branches (MainActivity.kt:177, 192, 204), on
every recomposition; `WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService
.onComplicationRequest` calls the same method synchronously
(WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService.kt:39); and
`ProfileSyncListenerService.onMessageReceived` calls it synchronously
too, before launching its own coroutine
(ProfileSyncListenerService.kt:42). None of these three are inside the
lock currently, but all three block on it — on the main thread for the
first two — for as long as `markSegment`'s `runBlocking` holds it.

`markSegment`'s own contract, in `RaceRecordingRepository.kt`, promises
`Result<Race>`. The `runBlocking` block sits inside a plain function
body with no `try`/`catch` around it: an exception raised while
collecting the profile flow — or by `CorrectionFactorCalculator
.compute` — propagates straight out of `markSegment`, past the
`Result.success(updated)` on its last line, and is never the
`Result.failure` the interface documents.

## Expected

`markSegment` never blocks a thread waiting on the profile flow and
never holds a lock across a suspension: it reads the profile with a
plain suspend call — `profileRepository.observe().first()`, without
`runBlocking` — in the coroutine its caller already runs in. Every
method of `RaceRecordingRepository` that touches shared state does the
same: the state is protected without blocking a thread across a
suspension point (a `Mutex` held only across the synchronous part of
each method, or another non-blocking scheme), so `findInProgress`,
called from the composable body, the complication service and the
sync listener, never waits on `markSegment`'s database read. An
exception raised while reading the profile or computing the correction
factor is caught inside `markSegment` and returned as `Result.failure`,
never allowed to propagate past the method's own return.

**Second gap — the interface signature.** `RaceRecordingRepository`
declares every method, including `markSegment` and `findInProgress`,
as a plain (non-`suspend`) function; `RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl`
cannot read the profile as a suspension without either `markSegment`
becoming `suspend` or the profile being obtained through another
non-blocking path. Making `markSegment` (and, if the same non-blocking
discipline is applied throughout, `findInProgress`) a `suspend`
function is a change to `RaceRecordingRepository` itself, and every
caller of the changed methods must be re-read against it:

- `SegmentMarkingController.onPressEnd` (SegmentMarkingController.kt)
  is a plain function today; if `markSegment` becomes `suspend`,
  `onPressEnd` must become `suspend` too, and its own callers —
  the race screens' ViewModels — already run it in `viewModelScope`,
  so they accept a suspend call.
- `RaceLaunchController.openPreparation` (RaceLaunchController.kt:22)
  already calls `findInProgress()` from inside a `suspend fun`, so a
  `suspend findInProgress()` fits it unchanged.
- `WatchApp`'s composable body (MainActivity.kt:177, 192, 204) calls
  `findInProgress()` directly at composition time, not inside a
  coroutine at all: a `suspend` `findInProgress()` cannot be called
  there as written. This is the gap the bug list also states
  separately (`WatchApp` reads a repository on every recomposition):
  the composable needs `produceState`, `LaunchedEffect` or an
  equivalent to collect the suspend call and remember its result.
- `WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService.onComplicationRequest`
  (WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService.kt:35-56) is a
  platform-declared callback, not `suspend`, and calls
  `listener.onComplicationData(...)` synchronously after reading
  `findInProgress()`. A `suspend` `findInProgress()` cannot be called
  there as written either: the service needs its own coroutine scope,
  launched inside `onComplicationRequest`, that calls
  `listener.onComplicationData(...)` once the suspend call returns.
- `ProfileSyncListenerService.onMessageReceived` (line 42) calls
  `findInProgress()` synchronously, ahead of the `serviceScope.launch`
  it already opens two lines later. A `suspend` `findInProgress()`
  cannot be called there as written: the call must move inside the
  existing `launch` block, alongside `profileSyncPushService
  .applyIncoming`.
